Music
At Clifton Hampden Primary School we aim to make music an enjoyable experience. We encourage the children to participate in a variety of musical experiences through which we aim to build up their love of music, self-confidence and sense of achievement. Our teaching focuses on developing the children's ability to sing in tune and with other people, play tuned and untuned musical instruments with increasing control, fluency and expression and listen to a wide range of music from different periods, genres, styles and traditions. Children will explore how music is created, produced and communicated and will improvise and compose music for a range of purposes.

pageCache.text:
Clifton Hampden, Abingdon, OX14 3EE
Personal, Social & Health Education
PSHE/RSE Curriculum Intent
At Clifton Hampden CE Primary School, we use Jigsaw as a whole school approach to deliver Personal, Social, Health and Economic education (PSHE) as well as Relationships and Sex Education (RSE). Jigsaw offers us a comprehensive, carefully thought through scheme of work that brings both consistency and progression to our children’s learning whilst supporting our school vision.
There is a strong emphasis on emotional literacy, building resilience and nurturing mental health, whilst developing the ‘whole’ child morally, socially and spiritually. The Jigsaw approach enables children to identify their feelings and emotions and regulate their own behaviour. Through our PSHE curriculum, pupils have the opportunity to acquire the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to keep themselves healthy and safe, respect and understand who they are and empower them with a voice to equip them for modern life so they can make a meaningful contribution to society.
In the Early Years, personal, social and emotional development is a prime area and is part of each child’s continuous provision. Throughout Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2, PSHE (Jigsaw) is mostly delivered in weekly sessions; however some units are delivered in blocks. There are six Jigsaw puzzles (termly units) designed so that the whole school can study the same learning themes at the same time, at their own level. The ‘puzzles’ are sequential and developmental over a two-year cycle to account for mixed age classes.
The six themes are as follows:
Sometimes external agencies engage with our pupils to consolidate and extend their learning e.g. Junior Citizen and IMPS (Injury Minimisation Programme for Schools).
*We use strategies from the NASEN guidance/SENDCO/Ed. Phsych. to support our scaffolding within PHSE (Jigsaw). This might include:
Although RSHE is a common theme, explored in most puzzles, sex education is predominantly taught in puzzle 6 ‘Changing Me’.
“Today’s children and young people are growing up in an increasingly complex world and living their lives seamlessly on and offline. This presents many positive and exciting opportunities, but also challenges and risks. In this environment, children and young people need to know how to be safe and healthy, and how to manage their academic, personal and social lives in a positive way.”
“This is why we have made Relationships Education compulsory in all primary schools in England…as well as making Health Education compulsory in all state-funded schools.”
Secretary of State Foreword DfE Guidance 2019 p.4-5
PSHE education helps pupils to aspire, believe, explore and achieve their academic potential and develop the social skills they will need in later life. Our RSHE curriculum promotes safe, equal, caring and enjoyable relationships and provides the children with honest and accurate information so that they can learn about their bodies and sexual and reproductive health in ways that are age appropriate. It fosters gender and LGBT+ equality and challenges all forms of discrimination.
By the time children leave us for secondary school, they will have an enthusiasm and willingness to face new challenges; an understanding of how to push themselves, to be resilient and to persevere; they will have high self-esteem and show respect for the rights and feelings of others in our diverse society; they will have a good understanding of how to keep themselves safe, healthy and develop positive relationships as they become valued local and global citizens.

Our Governors
Clifton Hampden Church of England Primary School has a single governing body consisting of twelve governors representing parents, teachers, local government, the Church and the local community. They all work in a voluntary capacity and their time and expertise is greatly appreciated. The powers and duties of governors are prescribed by law and they endeavor to ensure that schools conduct their affairs in accordance with all relevant legal obligations.
Aims of the Governing Body:
The main aim of the Governing Body is to hold the schools leadership team to account to ensure that all strategic decisions are made in the best interests of the children. Governors are responsible for: ensuring that the National Curriculum is delivered; monitoring the school’s performance and progress; ensuring the effective use of school funds; and setting the direction for future development. Governors play an active part in self-evaluating the schools performance and developing and monitoring school improvement initiatives to ensure they are impactful and making a difference to children. Governors are responsible for recruiting the Head Teacher and are often involved in staffing decisions, such as the selection of new staff.
The governors also monitor:
Governors view their role as one of partnership with parents and teachers for the ultimate benefit of all the children who attend Clifton Hampden Primary School.

No financial or business interests have been declared by the governors and none of the governors are related to members of staff.

Attendance
At Clifton Hampden CE Primary School, we expect the highest possible level of attendance. Our aim is to ensure that all pupils make excellent progress, achieve high levels of attainment and develop positive relationships with both staff and other pupils. This is achievable only when pupils are present for every possible session. Our aim is to work alongside pupils and parents/carers to promote, support and when necessary involve the Local Authority to ensure that each pupil is receiving their education.
The school day begins at 8.45am and we expect parents to help their child to be punctual.
When your children arrives late at school, they miss out on important information.
Your child may also feel embarrassed at having to enter the classroom late.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clifton Hampden CE Primary School - School Meals
pageCache.text:
Clifton Hampden, Abingdon, OX14 3EE
School Meals
Nourishing school lunches are cooked off site and supplied hot and fresh by John Mason catering team. A menu is sent each season and parents may order their child a lunch as little or as often as they wish. The cost of lunch for paying participants is currently £3.25 per day. All food is sourced locally where possible and cooked fresh on their site.
Please find the current school menu here
The menu may change to meet local preferences. There is always a jacket potato with filling option available daily.
John Mason catering team are committed to providing meals for children needing special diets for medical and cultural reasons, where possible. Please let us know if your child requires a special diet.
UNIVERSAL INFANT FREE SCHOOL MEALS
The universal infant free school meals policy, launched in September 2014, entitles every child in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 to a free lunch at school every day.
If you are not yet taking up this offer - or if your child is in Years 3 - 6 and not having school lunches, you may be interested in reading this article from The Independent School Food Plan
FREE SCHOOL MEALS (FSM)
Your child may be entitled to Free School Meals if your family is on low income or in receipt of state benefits or Universal Credit.
https://www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/residents/schools/school/school-meals If you think you may qualify, please contact the school office for advice on how to apply. Any communication / correspondence in this regard is handled with sensitivity and confidentiality.
School lunches are ordered a week in advance to allow the caterers to confirm their orders with their suppliers. Orders for Preschool and KS2 children are made via Parentmail PMX in your accounts tab. Ordering deadline is by Thursday for the following week.
Reception & KS1 children are strongly encouraged to take up their Universal Free School Meal and they are opted in as default, so please confirm with the school office if your child will be bringing in a packed lunch.
Lunch payments are made online via Parent Pay in your PMX Parentmail account.
If you provide your children with a packed lunch from home, please ensure that the lunches are healthy to help us encourage good health & dental hygiene.
No sweets or fizzy drinks please, these items are not permitted to be consumed in school. We are an allergy aware school so please do not include any nuts or products containing nuts in your child's lunch box, as these cannot be consumed in school.
For help and ideas visit: https://www.nhs.uk/healthier-families/recipes/healthier-lunchboxes/

pageCache.pageTitle: Clifton Hampden CE Primary School - School Uniform
pageCache.text:
Clifton Hampden, Abingdon, OX14 3EE
School Uniform
Uniform Examples
*School uniform is not compulsory for our preschool children (Tadpoles).
It is compulsory for our primary children to be supported to always wear school uniform. School uniform is important for a variety of reasons: It reduces competition and peer pressure among pupils, it helps to keep the focus on education and learning as opposed to fashion choices, and it reduces clothing expenses for all parents. Wearing a uniform helps to instil a sense of school pride and belonging, and therefore we ask that you support us in promoting this with your child. Pupil Premium children can be supported with purchasing uniform items.
NB: Please only send your child in lace up shoes if they can tie their own laces.
Please label all items of clothing & uniform clearly with your child’s name.
You can obtain the Clifton Hampden uniform from Brigade who provide an online ordering service, or most high street retailers stock uniform items that match our requirements.
http://www.brigade.uk.com/
Any items ordered can be delivered into school (free p&p) or to your door (p&p chargeable).
Daily outer wear requirements
Your child will need a coat/rain mac and appropriate footwear every day. Please provide a pair of wellington boots that can be left at school for outdoor activities and Forest School. hats, gloves & scarves are also required throughout winter.
During the warmer months, your child will require a sun hat in school daily for any outdoor play / Forest School sessions.
While we recommend an all-day suncream to be applied at home before the school day, KS2 children in years 3-6 are permitted to bring their own suncream into school (to be kept in their book bags) for self-re-application as necessary.
The wearing of a single pair of small stud earrings is permitted, however these must be removed or taped over for PE and Swimming. A wristwatch may be worn but must be removed for sports. The school cannot accept responsibility for loss or damage of personal items of this regard. No other jewellery is permitted to be worn in school. Hair that is long enough to be tied back, must always be tied back.
Clifton Hampden, Abingdon, OX14 3EE
